newsitem.title: USA: GM courts South Florida Hispanic market.
newsitem.headline: GM courts South Florida Hispanic market.

text.p: General Motors Corp, which once sold itself as American as baseball, hot dogs and apple pie, is now looking to salsa, the Macarena and soccer to drive forward sales in South Florida.

Aware of the need to woo the Hispanic market, GM Corp is sponsoring a day of fesitivities at Miami's South Beach on March 2 as part of the city's Carnaval -- the biggest Latin festival in the United States.
The event is a showcase for GM's efforts to catch up in a market where it has lagged behind as the spending power of south Florida's Hispanic community has grown.
"We've got to boost the South Florida market with more velocity than before," Knox Ramsey, GM executive director for regional markets, told Reuters.
"We think Carnaval has a lot of potential in overall visibility. We'll have the opportunity to display our cars all day and have them in the parade. It seemed like a nice fit."
Hispanics now make up at least 55 per cent of greater Miami's population and a significant part of South Florida's.
"That translates into the majority of people who are looking to buy an automobile," Ramsey said.

Marketing executives say GM had been slow to wake up to the spending power of Hispanics. GM has about 31 percent of the total U.S. market but a South Florida share of only about 17 percent, with a Hispanic market share of 16 percent.

"The Hispanic community came of economic age in the 1970s. It has a loyalty to Japanese cars, which are good value and are very reliable. Ford (Motor Co is) also very strong here," said Steve Blanco of Accentmarketing, which is handling the push. The strategy now aims to hit regional markets, he said.
John Maciarz, GM's regional communications manager for the southern region, conceded that GM had not been in top gear in the area. "We need to do a better job," he said.
"Carnaval is an opportunity to do things better and differently. We wanted to shake off our somewhat staid and conservative image. We want to be associated with a good time."
The South Beach event will feature a parade, soccer matches, and Latin bands and dancing -- including an attempt to break the world record for the number of people dancing the Macarena.
GM will also display the 13 new models it is introducing this year -- among them the Chevrolet Malibu, the Buick Park Avenue Ultra and the Cadillac Catera.
The new effort in South Florida also involves strengthening dealerships by signing up more Hispanic dealers.
